items.rationale: (a) closes every state where no cap runs today without overriding the owner's ruled anchor for triggered stops. (b) would fire earlier than the owner's ruled triggered-stop anchor in a gap, overriding a standing ruling. (c) replaces the owner's chosen fixed M.SL distance with a new parameter the owner has not asked for.
items.question: Before a stop triggers, or with no stop at all, nothing caps the loss of an open position; the M.SL emergency only runs after the exchange triggers the stop, and its anchor rule (top-of-book at the first reposition) was set by the owner. What should a new position-level loss cap do?

options.text: Backstop only: flatten when the price is one M.SL past the position's stop trigger AND the triggered-stop M.SL path is not running (no stop, stop untriggered past its trigger, stop rejected, restart before the snapshot); same M.SL setting; existing emergency sequence.
options.label: (a)

options.text: Always armed from the trigger, also while the triggered-stop M.SL path runs.
options.label: (b)

options.text: Scaled to ATR (k x ATR) instead of the M.SL setting.
options.label: (c)

items.rationale: M.SL off is the owner's explicit choice; a separate always-on cap would bring back a cap the owner turned off. (a) keeps one switch and makes the gap visible by a page. (b) protects more but adds a second, overlapping setting.
items.id: docs/spec-protection-batch3.md|B3-R2 cap when M.SL is off@033b8e0
items.question: The owner can untick the M.SL emergency or set it to 0. Should the new position-level loss cap also be off then?

options.text: Off too, and page once per position that it has no loss cap.
options.label: (a)

options.text: A separate cap setting that stays on even when M.SL is off.
options.label: (b)

items.rationale: (a) restores live data quickly and stops new signal-driven entries while blind; cancel-on-disconnect is off so a reconnect deletes nothing. (b) is simpler but leaves the app blind until the owner acts.
items.question: The app treats an open socket as connected and has no measure of silence, so a stalled feed (no frames, socket still open) goes unnoticed while a position or working entry exists. What should happen on a detected stall?

options.text: Probe with public/test after 3 s with no inbound frame; no reply in 2 s means a stall: urgent page, the bridge refuses new acts, and the app forces a reconnect.
options.label: (a)

items.rationale: A stand-down that keeps an entry working still acts on the old signal. (b) leaves a stale order resting. (c) needs a shared-schema change the app cannot make alone; (a) is the app's full half of it.
items.question: When the engine stands down (stale payload, SKIPPED, ARM off), a working entry placed by the bridge keeps being chased and its abort cap can even be widened. What should a stand-down do?

options.text: Cancel the bridge-placed working entry (scoped cancel); stand-down payloads never resize its abort cap; manual entries untouched.
options.label: (a)

options.text: Freeze the entry: stop chasing and keep the cap.
options.label: (b)

options.text: (a) plus publish the working entry in the shared feedback file for the engine (needs the engine side; deferred).
options.label: (c)

items.rationale: (a) keeps the engine's field meaningful within a bound the app controls. (b) discards information. (c) leaves the payload judging itself.
items.question: A payload is judged fresh against a window computed from a field the payload itself carries (2.5 x exec_resolution_min minutes, no upper bound). How should the app bound it?

options.text: Cap it: 2.5 x min(exec_resolution_min, N) minutes, N a setting with default 1; escalate first if the engine emits values above 1.
options.label: (a)

options.text: Use the app's own fixed window and ignore the payload's field.
options.label: (b)
